pr_title: ServerSentEvents: Support CRLF + LF as line endings
pr_body:
# ServerSentEvents: Support CRLF + LF as line endings

MessageParser now allows a combination of CRLF and LF.

## Description

This PR updates the ServerSentEvent MessageParser to support single LF tokens instead of only a CRLF combination.

This change was made so that different servers libraries that only send `\n` line delimitted messages are supported.

Additionally the documentation should be updated

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/src/SignalR/docs/specs/TransportProtocols.md#server-sent-events-server-to-client-only

> [...] The server transmits frames as "events" using the SSE protocol. The protocol encodes a single event as a sequence of key-value pair lines, separated by : and using any of \r\n, \n or \r as line-terminators, followed by a final blank line.

Other references:

https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html#parsing-an-event-stream

> Lines must be separated by either a U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN U+000A LINE FEED (CRLF) character pair, a single U+000A LINE FEED (LF) character, or a single U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) character.

Fixes #42001

pr_comments: Thanks for your PR, @kirides. Someone from the team will get assigned to your PR shortly and we'll get it reviewed.

Implementation was changed to reflect current decisions.

for now only line buffered formats (`\r\n` & `\n`) are supported.
`\r` is not planned yet, due to complexity and possible delays  
Someone might send `data: hello\r` leaving us having to buffer until we have atleast another byte, worst case two bytes:
`\r` may be followed by ...
1. `\n` for line buffering
2. `\r` meaning current line is complete, wait for next byte to check if we're at end of message, as the second `\r` might just aswell be a part of `\r\n`
3. any other byte, which would mean current line is completed, start next line.

> 2\. `\r` meaning current line is complete, wait for next byte to check if we're at end of message, as the second `\r` might just aswell be a part of `\r\n`

This sounds almost like `\r` is supported since we're delaying for more bytes 😆 
Now I'm wondering how much extra code it would actually be to support `\r`...

> > 2. `\r` meaning current line is complete, wait for next byte to check if we're at end of message, as the second `\r` might just aswell be a part of `\r\n`
> 
> This sounds almost like `\r` is supported since we're delaying for more bytes 😆 Now I'm wondering how much extra code it would actually be to support `\r`...

With the current proposed implementation, `\r` is "accepted" as valid data if not followed immediately by a `\n`, otherwise it counts towards the CRLF -> EOL.

for a "full" implementation, we would have to handle the following case in some way

```
data: something\r\r
```

if now the server doesn't send any more bytes, how would we know if the `data` is complete?
worst case, we would have to wait until the server closes the connection and accept it as `EOL`.

Looks like this PR hasn't been active for some time and the codebase could have been changed in the meantime.
To make sure no conflicting changes have occurred, please rerun validation before merging. You can do this by leaving an `/azp run` comment here (requires commit rights), or by simply closing and reopening.
Sorry it took so long, thanks for the fix @kirides
Thanks a lot for the merge!

issue_context.title: SignalR Client ServerSentEvents does not support `\n` delimited Messages
issue_context.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

A SignalR Server implementation that writes SSE Messages delimited by `\n` breaks `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.Connections.Client.Internal.ServerSentEventsMessageParser.ParseMessage`
( [source.dot.net ParseMessage#74](https://source.dot.net/#Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.Connections.Client/Internal/ServerSentEventsMessageParser.cs,74) )


```
FormatException:
Unexpected '\n' in message. A '\n' character can only be used as part of the newline sequence '\r\n'
```

Tested NuGets:

`Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Client`
- 5.0.0
- 6.0.5
- 7.0.0-preview.4.22251.1 

### Expected Behavior

`ServerSentEventsMessageParser.ParseMessage` supports messages delimited by any of `\r`, `\n`, `\r\n` as mentioned in the spec

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/src/SignalR/docs/specs/TransportProtocols.md#server-sent-events-server-to-client-only

> [...] The server transmits frames as "events" using the SSE protocol. The protocol encodes a single event as a sequence of key-value pair lines, separated by : and using any of \r\n, \n or \r as line-terminators, followed by a final blank line.

Other references:

https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html#parsing-an-event-stream

> Lines must be separated by either a U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN U+000A LINE FEED (CRLF) character pair, a single U+000A LINE FEED (LF) character, or a single U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) character.


### Steps To Reproduce

```cs
var client = new Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Client.HubConnectionBuilder()
	.AddJsonProtocol()
	.WithAutomaticReconnect()
	.WithUrl("http://127.0.0.1:5987/notifications")
	.Build();

await client.StartAsync();
// Exception is thrown
```

Server gist (Go):  https://gist.github.com/kirides/2743b09da0b3f4b6bd5d501e60bd0324


### Exceptions (if any)

_No response_

### .NET Version

6.0.203

### Anything else?

_No response_

review_comments: This was removed as we can't really get to `0` chars, due to line being always atleast `\n`

We have no way to distinguish between messages when reading. That means
`"data: ", "Hello", "
"` would behave differently than `"data: ", "Hello
"`

This is on the client, so it's less concerning. But it does feel like we're making the client flaky. I wonder if we can compromise and accept `
` or `
` and not support just ``.

Either we have to absolutely read the next byte (s) to ensure a complete line (more complexity) or just accept that hopefully people either use Unix or windows line endings.

This would mean that we also need to adjust the docs to clarify that we only support a subset of the SSE line endings.

For my use cases accepting just \\n and not \\r would be enough

> Either we have to absolutely read the next byte (s) to ensure a complete line (more complexity)

I think this is what the spec is referring to here:

"while line buffering with lines are defined to end with a single U+000A LINE FEED (LF) character is safe, block buffering or line buffering with different expected line endings can cause delays in event dispatch."

I think adding `\n` to our current support is good enough. And we should update the SignalR spec.

Do you think the implementation should trim any trailing `\r`?
for cases like `data: \r\r\n`, which would result in `data: \r`
